page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan. Left page: one text column with running head and page number at the top; no margin notes. Right page: a narrow strip at the right edge showing the beginning of a neighbouring column (partly cut off), which is a margin of the facing page and is not transcribed in full. The main text is one column on the left printed page, ending with a heading, a short italic maxim and "Exemplo" at the foot.

main_text.p: sanctarentur, & ne respub. cogeretur alere pigros ventres. Vtinam vero hodie etiam in ociosos lex statuatur, sicut olim Romæ censoribus id negocium datum fuit, ne quis ociosus in vrbe oberraret; vnde multa bona redundarent in rempubl. & inter alia hoc etiã, quod tali in ociosos inquisitione magna sæpe sceleta detegantur, vt egregiè de hac re difcurrit Camerarius parte 1. Medit. hiftor. c. 15. Et sane ocium cum sit ἀργία quædam contra legem & voluntatē Dei, qui vult vt homines in sudore vultus sui sustentationem vitæ quærat, vtque non laborantes non manducent, idcirco facilè rerumpublic. mutationem multitudo ocioforum hominum causare poteft ; quod & Lipf.lib.4. cap. 11. annotauit, vbi citat verba Sallustii ad Cæsarem: Curabit princeps vt quilibet habeat negocia sua, quibus à malo publico retineatur. Vide Plat.libr.11. De legibus, Bodin. lib. 5. cap.2. Tolof.lib.22.cap.7. vbi egregiè describit occupationes, quas princeps ociosis demandare possit. Vide etiam Aretium tomo 2.problem.loco 140. Memorabilis est sententia Gersonis in opuf. de remediis contra pusillanimitatem, vbi inquit: Cor ociosi hominis est instar molendini, quod cum non habet ad molendum bonum frumentum; quia in continuo motu est, molit & consumit seipsum.
main_text.head: De cura tolerantiæ & fortitudinis hi sunt Canones:

p.i: Ad tolerantiam & fortitudinem subditos suos princeps à prima ætate publicis quibusdã exercitiis assuefaciat.

page.notes: The printed page number is "416" with the running head "SYSTEMATIS POLITICI"; the numeral as printed reads "416" and is uncertain at the first digit. Left margin has no notes. The right-hand strip is cut off and only fragments are legible; it was not transcribed. Several words in the text are doubtful (e.g. "sceleta", "quærat", "ἀργία" is a reading of a Greek word, uncertain). The Greek word in the printed text may differ.
